label: generate-trigger-index.mjs --check exits 1 on a clean checkout: 43 of 43 rows are documents ADDED since the index build (including the research packet's own spec, tasks, timeline and decision-record), all bucketed under one verdict whose summary says 'missing from the index' while each row says 'stale'; the lookup emits no stale boolean (grep 'stale' in lookup-trigger-index.mjs is empty) and prints an unverified claim that 'no lookup answer depends on it' for the manifest mismatch, so Gate 1 has no way to see freshness

runtime/data/trigger-index.json is rebuilt in every release at roughly 50k lines a time (numstat +47952/-45440, +49505/-46644, +59675/-52086, +54271/-50889 across v4.0.0.15, v4.0.0.16, v4.0.1.0, v4.0.2.0) because it re-encodes every document's phrases; nothing breaks if it is left alone since the build is deterministic and measure-cold-lookup.mjs already exists to price a cold start

MEASURED_BEHAVIOR is correctly wired (validator-registry.json rule_id row plus orchestrator dispatch of rules/*.sh through bash) but rules/check-measured-behavior.sh only defines functions and the RULE_* contract, so executed standalone it prints nothing and exits 0 even for a packet whose measured-behavior block is empty; severity is warn and the script can never report fail, so an author following the v4.0.0.15 'one strict run, fix everything' card gets a silent green script

The measured-behavior block ships in templates/core/spec.md.tmpl with an anchor, and the stamp is spec-core | v2.4, exactly the rule's MIN_MAJOR/MIN_MINOR floor, so the rule applies to every newly scaffolded packet from its first second while the block is by definition unfilled (a fenced placeholder does not count as filled because unfilled value tokens are excluded) - a warn the author cannot clear at creation time

create.sh has no --dry-run or --preview (help lists --phase, --phases, --phase-names, --parent, --phase-parent, --path, --track only) yet it is the one tool in this cluster whose whole job is to write, and v4.0.2.0 added four more write paths to it via refresh_track_level and inspect_subtrack; the Q7 claim therefore cannot be tested by a read-only research run or by CI, only by writing a packet

Decision capture's operational facts are note-only: SKILL.md:146 and references/memory/save-workflow.md:278 document that a --full-auto save writes operatorDecisions into decision-record.md, but SYSTEM_DECISION_CAPTURE_DISABLED=1, the Claude Code /hooks approval or restart requirement and the per-linked-project cleanup save appear only in the v4.0.1.0 changelog (lines 114, 189, 190) - a grep of the skill docs for the switch returns zero hits

The v4.0.2.0 upgrade note tells operators to run 'npm run build' in .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime to use the history lookup, but the compiled artifact already ships at runtime/dist/hooks/lib/history/cli.js, so the step is a contributor step presented as user setup and it contradicts validate.sh's own refusal to run against a stale compiled orchestrator

v4.0.0.16's entire spec-kit surface delta is a three-line deletion in create.sh that removes the phase-context Changelog block from a new phase child; the fix is correct because the scaffolded instruction pointed at a folder the skill no longer owns, and it is recorded so the release is not miscounted as a surface change

direction: create.sh silently creates a packet inside an undeclared sub-track because is_declared_subtrack discards stdout and refresh_track_root returns 0
reason: The --track guard runs before any mkdir and refuses outright, printing the diagnostic captured through subtrack_diagnostic; refresh_track_root is only reached on the accepted path, so the silent skip is a defensive branch and not reachable for a --track value

direction: The token '3' being below MIN_TOKEN_LENGTH makes the phrase 'gate 3' unmatchable in the trigger index
reason: The lookup does discard it, but the query still returned the gate-3 packet at rank 2 with matchClass query-containment and score 0.88, and the index holds 'gate 3' phrases such as 'claude gate 3 classifier'
